answer: A sybil defense can use longitudinal consistency checks: every agent builds a public trail of verified tasks over months, and at dawn of each audit window it must complete a new task that builds directly on its own past work, like continuing a sonnet it started rather than reciting a fresh one. A single operator spinning up many identities faces a cost that grows with each fake history, because keeping dozens of timelines coherent, distinct, and progressing toward the same horizon is far more expensive than faking one profile once. Inconsistent or copy-paste histories lose their standing.
